main_point.en: Faith is believing Jesus’s words before seeing His works.
main_point.zh-Hant: 信心就是在看見耶穌的作為以前，相信祂的話。

christ_connection.en: Jesus responded to those who came to Him in faith for physical healing. In a greater way, all who come to Jesus in faith for salvation from sin are forgiven and restored with God.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 耶穌回應那些憑信心來求祂醫治身體的人。更重要的是，凡憑信心來到耶穌面前，尋求脫離罪的拯救的人，都得蒙赦免，與神和好。

title.zh-Hant: 絕境引領我們來到耶穌面前

content.en:
46 So he came again to Cana in Galilee, where he had made the water wine. And at Capernaum there was an official whose son was ill.
47 When this man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and asked him to come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death.
48 So Jesus said to him, “Unless you see signs and wonders you will not believe.”
content.zh-Hant:
46 耶穌又到了加利利的迦拿，就是他從前變水為酒的地方。有一個大臣，他的兒子在迦百農患病。
47 他聽見耶穌從猶太到了加利利，就來見他，求他下去醫治他的兒子，因為他兒子快要死了。
48 耶穌就對他說：「若不看見神蹟奇事，你們總是不信。」

content.en:
49 The official said to him, “Sir, come down before my child dies.”
50 Jesus said to him, “Go; your son will live.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and went on his way.
51 As he was going down, his servants met him and told him that his son was recovering.
52 So he asked them the hour when he began to get better, and they said to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”
53 The father knew that was the hour when Jesus had said to him, “Your son will live.” And he himself believed, and all his household.
54 This was now the second sign that Jesus did when he had come from Judea to Galilee.
content.zh-Hant:
49 那大臣說：「先生，求你趁著我的孩子還沒有死就下去。」
50 耶穌對他說：「回去吧，你的兒子活了！」那人信耶穌所說的話就回去了。
51 正下去的時候，他的僕人迎見他，說他的兒子活了。
52 他就問甚麼時候見好的。他們說：「昨日未時熱就退了。」
53 他便知道這正是耶穌對他說「你兒子活了」的時候；他自己和全家就都信了。
54 這是耶穌在加利利行的第二件神蹟，是他從猶太回去以後行的。

content.en: Leaders: Spend time reflecting on how Jesus’s works have strengthened your belief. Our faith is steady and sure, rooted in hope and in proof of what we haven’t yet seen (Heb. 11:1).
content.zh-Hant: 帶領者：花時間思想耶穌的作為如何堅固你的信心。我們的信心穩固而確實，根植於盼望，也是我們尚未看見之事的憑據（來 11:1）。

title.zh-Hant: 絕境引領我們來到耶穌面前

content.en: “This official could be either a Jew or a Gentile, and if he was a Gentile, then the divine grace revealed in this story is even more remarkable. But John does not indicate that the official is a Gentile, so we cannot be certain. In any case, for many Jews a servant at Herod’s court would be little better than a Gentile, so the scandalous nature of God’s grace is evident here even if the official is a Jew.”¹
content.zh-Hant: 「這位大臣可能是猶太人，也可能是外邦人；如果他是外邦人，這個故事中所顯明的神的恩典就更加不可思議。但約翰沒有表明他是外邦人，因此我們無法確定。無論如何，對許多猶太人來說，在希律王宮中服事的人不會比外邦人好多少；因此，即使這位大臣是猶太人，神的恩典令人震驚之處在這裏仍然顯而易見。」¹

content.en: “The word ‘go’ is imperative, so the man has been commanded by the Savior of the world with a promise of life for his son. But if he left, according to his way of thinking, he would leave behind his one chance for help. Jesus demanded that his faith be desperate enough to trust his word, not just his visible works. Wonders may produce awe, but words produce faith.”²
content.zh-Hant: 「『回去吧』是命令語氣，因此這人接到世人救主的命令，同時得到兒子會活的應許。但按他的想法，如果他離開，就會失去唯一得到幫助的機會。耶穌要求他在絕境中的信心足以信靠祂的話，而不只是祂看得見的作為。奇事可能產生敬畏，話語卻能產生信心。」²

content.en: “The man obeyed the word of Jesus without seeing the sign. In the ancient world miracles and acts of power were linked to the presence of the miracle worker, but here the healer refused to be present. The story therefore is an important illustration of the purpose for which John wrote the Gospel. Here believing the word is linked with not immediately seeing the sign.”³
content.zh-Hant: 「這人還沒有看見神蹟，就遵從了耶穌的話。在古代世界，神蹟和大能的作為都與行神蹟者親自在場有關，但在這裏，醫治者拒絕親自前往。因此，這個故事重要地說明了約翰寫福音書的目的。在這裏，相信話語與沒有立即看見神蹟連在一起。」³

content.en: According to the Gospel of John, Jesus performed two significant miracles in the town of Cana. The first miracle took place at the wedding where Jesus turned water into wine (John 2:1-11). After Jesus traveled through Judea and Samaria, He returned to Cana, where He performed a second miracle—the healing of the royal official’s son. Many biblical scholars believe this royal official was one of Herod’s officers who had heard of Jesus’s first miracle in Cana and then desperately pursued Jesus to help his sick son.⁴ The fact that the official asked Jesus to “come down” (4:47) and heal his son is consistent with the geography of the region: Cana is at a higher elevation in the hills, where Capernaum is down on the shore of the Sea of Galilee. Coming from Capernaum, the official would have traveled between 18 to 22 miles to reach Jesus in Cana. Verses 51-52 indicate that the official likely walked this long distance to Cana and back, given that he returned to his servants the day after he encountered Jesus.⁵ The official would have had many hours to think as he walked the dusty roads, desperately hoping that Jesus really would heal his son.
content.zh-Hant: 根據約翰福音，耶穌在迦拿鎮行了兩個重要的神蹟。第一個神蹟發生在婚宴上，耶穌把水變成酒（約 2:1-11）。耶穌經過猶太和撒馬利亞後，回到迦拿，在那裏行了第二個神蹟，就是醫治大臣的兒子。許多聖經學者認為，這位大臣是希律的一名官員；他聽說耶穌在迦拿行的第一個神蹟後，急切地尋求耶穌幫助他患病的兒子。⁴ 這位大臣求耶穌「下去」（4:47）醫治他兒子，與當地地形相符：迦拿位於較高的山區，迦百農則在較低的加利利海岸邊。這位大臣從迦百農出發，要走約十八至二十二英里才能到迦拿見耶穌。第 51 至 52 節指出，他很可能步行這段長路往返迦拿，因為他在遇見耶穌的第二天才與僕人會合。⁵ 大臣走在塵土飛揚的路上，有許多時間思考，迫切盼望耶穌真的會醫治他的兒子。

content.en: Justification refers to the moment when a person is declared righteous before God based on the righteousness of Jesus’s atoning death (Rom. 8:33-34). This act of declaration takes place through faith in Jesus and not as a result of human works or effort (Eph. 2:8-9). Through justification, a person is made to be in right standing before God, changing what was once a strained and hostile relationship to one of adoption into the family of God.
content.zh-Hant: 稱義是指一個人憑著耶穌贖罪之死的義，在神面前被宣告為義的時刻（羅 8:33-34）。這宣告是藉著相信耶穌而發生，並非出於人的行為或努力（弗 2:8-9）。藉著稱義，人得以在神面前有正確的地位，原本緊張、敵對的關係轉變為蒙接納進入神的家。

content.en: Lord, You are our great and powerful Healer. May we have confident faith in You, even when our perspectives are limited. Give us the strength and courage to walk by faith and not by sight. Please continue to grow our students’ faith as they pursue You.
content.zh-Hant: 主啊，祢是我們偉大而大有能力的醫治者。即使我們的眼光有限，願我們仍對祢有堅定的信心。求祢賜給我們力量和勇氣，行事憑著信心，不是憑著眼見。也求祢在學生追求祢的時候，繼續使他們的信心成長。

content.en: Did you know that the longest road in the world is nearly 19,000 miles long? The Pan-American Highway is made up of a series of roads that starts in Prudhoe Bay, Alaska, and stretches south to the tip of Argentina, the lower reaches of South America.⁶
content.zh-Hant: 你知道世界上最長的公路全長接近一萬九千英里嗎？泛美公路由一系列道路組成，從阿拉斯加的普拉德霍灣出發，向南延伸至阿根廷南端，也就是南美洲的南部。⁶

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You’ll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:
instructions.zh-Hant:
這些選用活動旨在幫助學生互動。當中包括討論活動和文化連結，後者涉及當今青少年文化中的相關話題。每個小組都不同，請調整這些活動以符合你的小組需要。目標是讓學生藉著與主題及彼此建立連結，更投入課程。

請提出以下問題，並留時間讓學生分享回答：

question.en: Who is the most powerful person you know?
question.zh-Hant: 你認識的人當中，誰最有能力？

question.en: Discuss a time you really needed someone’s help.
question.zh-Hant: 分享一次你非常需要別人幫助的經歷。

question.en: When have you hoped for something without knowing if it would happen?
question.zh-Hant: 你曾在不知道某件事會否發生的情況下盼望它成真嗎？

content.en: When Jesus began His public ministry and demonstrated His ability to perform miracles, people responded in a variety of ways. Some people suspected and doubted Him, while others believed in Him. We can trust in Jesus’s ability to work powerfully in our lives. He is our Redeemer, who has the power and desire to save all who come to Him in faith.
content.zh-Hant: 當耶穌開始公開事奉並展現行神蹟的能力時，人們的反應各不相同。有些人猜疑祂、懷疑祂，另一些人卻相信祂。我們可以信靠耶穌有能力在我們的生命中大大動工。祂是我們的救贖主，有能力也願意拯救所有憑信心來到祂面前的人。

cultural_connection.en: Have you ever wrestled with why God heals some people and not others? Christians aren’t immune to the effects of living in a fallen, broken world. Jesus often healed people’s sicknesses and diseases, and Scripture encourages us to pray for healing when we are sick (James 5:14,16). Sometimes God heals, but sometimes He chooses not to heal on this side of eternity. If you’ve walked through a situation where God didn’t answer a prayer for healing, you aren’t alone in feeling disappointed, hurt, or confused. We don’t have to hide our hurt or disappointment from God. Instead, we go to Him; we hold on to the truth that He is our good, loving Father, who uses everything—even what’s painful—to draw us close and make us more like Jesus (Rom. 8:28). We can invite Jesus into our suffering, knowing He sympathizes with our weaknesses and struggles because He also suffered here (Heb. 4:15). God always heals those who seek Him for spiritual healing. All who confess Jesus as Lord are saved (Rom. 10:9), and we have hope that no matter what happens on earth, we will spend eternity in heaven with no more pain, sickness, or disease.
cultural_connection.zh-Hant: 你是否曾為神為甚麼醫治一些人，卻不醫治另一些人而掙扎？基督徒生活在墮落、破碎的世界中，也不能免受其影響。耶穌常常醫治人的疾病，聖經也鼓勵我們生病時禱告求醫治（雅 5:14,16）。有時神會醫治，有時祂選擇在今生不予醫治。如果你曾經歷神沒有應允醫治禱告的處境，你並不是唯一感到失望、傷痛或困惑的人。我們不必向神隱藏傷痛或失望；相反，我們要來到祂面前，持守這真理：祂是良善、慈愛的天父，使用萬事，甚至痛苦的事，吸引我們親近祂，使我們更像耶穌（羅 8:28）。我們可以邀請耶穌進入我們的苦難，知道祂體恤我們的軟弱和掙扎，因為祂也曾在世上受苦（來 4:15）。神總會醫治那些向祂尋求屬靈醫治的人。凡承認耶穌為主的人都得救（羅 10:9）；我們有盼望，無論地上發生甚麼事，我們都會在天上度過永恆，不再有疼痛、病患和疾病。

title.zh-Hant: 絕境引領我們來到耶穌面前

question.en: What is the difference between needing something and being desperate for something? When have you felt desperate?
question.zh-Hant: 需要某樣東西與迫切渴求某樣東西有甚麼不同？你何時曾感到絕望無助？

answer.en: Leaders: Share context about distance from Capernaum to Cana. Desperation implies having an extreme and urgent need and may lead to risky or reckless behavior in an attempt to find answers. Maybe you’ve felt desperate for relief from pain or for a loved one’s healing. The royal official was clearly desperate to find healing for his sick son and traveled a long distance to seek Jesus’s help. Situations like these often lead us to Jesus when we realize we have nowhere else to turn. But the truth is that we can go to Jesus with every need because He cares about them all—both big and small.
answer.zh-Hant: 帶領者：分享從迦百農到迦拿的距離背景。絕境意味著有極大而迫切的需要，可能使人為了尋找答案而採取冒險或魯莽的行動。也許你曾迫切希望痛苦減輕，或盼望所愛的人得醫治。這位大臣顯然迫切希望患病的兒子得醫治，因此長途跋涉尋求耶穌幫助。這樣的處境常使我們意識到自己無處可去，因而來到耶穌面前。但事實是，我們可以帶著一切需要來到耶穌面前，因為無論大小，祂都關心。

question.en: How are we all in the same desperate situation before God? Why can’t we fix it?
question.zh-Hant: 我們所有人在神面前同樣身處甚麼絕境？為甚麼我們無法自行解決？

answer.en: We all have the same fundamental problem as human beings: We are spiritually dead because our sin separates us from God (Rom. 3:23; 6:23). We can’t earn salvation or forgiveness with our good works or by following God’s law. Because God is good, holy, and just, He can’t overlook sin or sweep it under the rug. This leaves us in a desperate situation because we are all guilty before God and deserving of death (John 3:18). Thankfully, God provided a way for us to be fully justified before Him through Jesus’s sacrificial death on our behalf. Jesus met us in our desperation and fixed what we couldn’t fix on our own.
answer.zh-Hant: 作為人類，我們都有同一個根本問題：我們在屬靈上是死的，因為我們的罪使我們與神隔絕（羅 3:23；6:23）。我們不能靠善行或遵守神的律法賺取救恩或赦免。因為神是良善、聖潔、公義的，祂不能忽視罪或將罪掩蓋。這使我們陷入絕境，因為我們在神面前都有罪，都該受死（約 3:18）。感謝神，祂藉著耶穌代替我們犧牲受死，為我們預備了一條在祂面前完全稱義的道路。耶穌在絕境中來到我們身邊，解決了我們自己無法解決的問題。

question.en: When we’re desperate, why do we often run to other things or people instead of Jesus? How does everything else fail us?
question.zh-Hant: 當我們陷入絕境時，為甚麼常轉向其他事物或人，而不是耶穌？其他一切如何使我們失望？

answer.en: Sometimes our earthly needs feel like the most significant issues we face. For example: We may feel desperate for belonging. And instead of seeking godly friends to walk with us, we settle for toxic friendships that distract us from following Jesus. To avoid loneliness, we settle for belonging in the wrong places. In our desperation, we often turn to other people or the things of this world instead of looking to God to rescue us or help us. However, no temporary solution can truly save us. No matter how great our earthly needs are, our spiritual need is greater. Jesus proved that He cares about our needs by coming to our broken world to save us from our sin. If we can trust Jesus with our greatest need—forgiveness of our sin—then we can trust Him to meet our other needs as well. Trusting Him with our eternal life means that we can also trust Him with our earthly life.
answer.zh-Hant: 有時我們覺得地上的需要是面對的最大問題。例如，我們可能迫切渴望歸屬感，卻沒有尋找敬虔的朋友同行，反而滿足於使我們分心、偏離跟隨耶穌之路的不健康友誼。為了避免孤單，我們在錯誤的地方尋求歸屬。身處絕境時，我們常轉向其他人或世上的事物，而不是仰望神拯救或幫助我們。然而，任何暫時的解決辦法都不能真正拯救我們。無論我們地上的需要有多大，屬靈的需要更大。耶穌來到我們破碎的世界，把我們從罪中拯救出來，證明祂關心我們的需要。如果我們能把最大的需要——罪得赦免——交託給耶穌，就也能信靠祂供應我們其他的需要。把永生交託給祂，也意味著我們能把地上的生命交託給祂。

question.en: How would you define genuine belief in Jesus?
question.zh-Hant: 你會如何定義對耶穌真正的信心？

answer.en: Genuine belief in Jesus involves both our head and our heart—our mind and our will. We must believe that He is the Son of God, sent to the world to save us from our sin. But only mentally acknowledging that Jesus is real is not enough to save us. The demons believe Jesus is real but do not follow Him (James 2:19). We must confess that Jesus is Lord and believe in our hearts that God raised Him from the dead (Rom. 10:9). Saving belief means that we believe in Jesus and obey what He says. Faith requires action. If we love Jesus, we must keep His commands (John 14:15). Just like the royal official believed and acted on what Jesus told him, we must do the same. True followers of Jesus must follow His commands to turn from our sinful ways and honor Him with our lives.
answer.zh-Hant: 真正相信耶穌同時涉及我們的頭腦和內心，也就是思想和意志。我們必須相信祂是神的兒子，被差到世上拯救我們脫離罪。但僅在理智上承認耶穌真實存在，並不足以使我們得救。鬼魔也相信耶穌是真實的，卻不跟隨祂（雅 2:19）。我們必須承認耶穌是主，並且心裏相信神使祂從死裏復活（羅 10:9）。使人得救的信心意味著我們相信耶穌，並遵行祂的話。信心需要行動。如果我們愛耶穌，就必須遵守祂的命令（約 14:15）。正如大臣相信耶穌對他說的話並付諸行動，我們也必須如此。真正跟隨耶穌的人必須遵行祂的命令，離棄罪惡的道路，以生命尊榮祂。

question.en: Why do you think we sometimes struggle to take Jesus at His word or to trust His promises?
question.zh-Hant: 你認為為甚麼我們有時難以相信耶穌所說的話或信靠祂的應許？

answer.en: Trusting people can be difficult if they’ve let you down or disappointed you. We more easily trust people when we see their good character. Thankfully, Jesus is perfectly trustworthy. Jesus wants us to take Him at His word, and He is kind enough to show us that we have good reasons to trust Him. Jesus backs up His words with action. He proved His power and authority by performing signs and miracles, like healing the royal official’s son. Jesus proved that He loves us by dying on the cross for our sins. He demonstrated His power as the Messiah through His death and resurrection, which He predicted beforehand. Jesus knows that our limited human perspective can make it difficult for us to trust Him, so we can look to His power and fulfilled promises to strengthen our faith.
answer.zh-Hant: 如果別人曾令你失望或辜負你，信任人可能很困難。當我們看見一個人的好品格，就較容易信任他。感謝神，耶穌完全值得信靠。耶穌希望我們相信祂的話，祂也慈愛地讓我們看見自己有充分的理由信靠祂。耶穌以行動印證祂的話。祂藉著行神蹟奇事，例如醫治大臣的兒子，證明了祂的能力和權柄。耶穌為我們的罪死在十字架上，證明祂愛我們。祂藉著自己事先預告的死亡和復活，彰顯了祂作為彌賽亞的能力。耶穌知道我們有限的眼光可能使我們難以信靠祂，因此我們可以仰望祂的能力和已經實現的應許，來堅固我們的信心。

question.en: What does Jesus’s ability and willingness to heal people like the royal official’s son reveal about Him?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌有能力也願意醫治像大臣兒子這樣的人，顯明了祂是怎樣的一位？

answer.en: Some scholars believe that the royal official wasn’t Jewish but a Roman Gentile. Jesus’s ability to heal shows that He is the Messiah, and His willingness to heal a Gentile shows that He loves and cares for all people. Not only did Jesus’s healings fulfill Old Testament prophecies about what the Messiah would do (Matt. 8:17), but they also showed us His heart. Jesus had compassion for those who were sick or struggling with sin and those who wanted to be near to Him. Jesus is gentle and lowly at heart (Matt. 11:29) and offers grace and mercy to those who come to Him. He is our kind and loving Savior, who laid down His life for us so that we could have fellowship with Him forever.
answer.zh-Hant: 有些學者認為，大臣不是猶太人，而是羅馬外邦人。耶穌醫治的能力顯明祂是彌賽亞，而祂願意醫治外邦人，顯明祂愛所有人、關心所有人。耶穌的醫治不僅應驗了舊約中關於彌賽亞所要做之事的預言（太 8:17），也向我們顯明祂的心。耶穌憐憫患病、與罪掙扎以及想親近祂的人。耶穌心裏柔和謙卑（太 11:29），並向來到祂面前的人施恩典和憐憫。祂是我們仁慈、慈愛的救主，為我們捨命，使我們可以永遠與祂相交。

question.en: In what situation is Jesus asking you to trust Him before seeing the results? What would it look like to have faith before seeing the outcome?
question.zh-Hant: 在甚麼情況下，耶穌要你在看見結果以前信靠祂？在看見結果以前有信心，會是甚麼樣子？

answer.en: When Jesus told the royal official that his son would live, the man believed Jesus would be true to His word. He made the long journey back to Capernaum, trusting Jesus had healed his son before seeing the proof. We are called to have this same confidence in Jesus’s words, but this can be challenging when we are in a season of waiting. Maybe you are waiting to find a solid group of friends. Maybe you’re waiting for a college admissions letter or a scholarship opportunity. Maybe you’re waiting to hear back from a doctor about test results. In the “in between” times, we are called to walk by faith and not by sight (2 Cor. 5:7)—to believe before we see. Knowing that we serve a powerful and merciful Savior is comforting. Jesus has already met our greatest need by providing the way for us to be restored to God. He promises to be with us and give us the strength we need to follow Him every day (Phil. 4:13). Remembering Jesus’s power and His love for us will help us trust Him while we wait to see the outcome.
answer.zh-Hant: 當耶穌告訴大臣他的兒子會活時，那人相信耶穌會履行祂的話。他踏上回迦百農的長路，在看見證據以前就相信耶穌已醫治他的兒子。我們蒙召同樣堅信耶穌的話，但在等待的時期，這可能很困難。也許你正等著找到一群可靠的朋友，也許你正等候大學錄取通知或獎學金機會，也許你正等醫生告知檢查結果。在這些「等待之間」的日子，我們蒙召行事憑著信心，不是憑著眼見（林後 5:7），在看見以前就相信。知道我們服事的是一位大有能力、充滿憐憫的救主，實在令人安慰。耶穌已經提供使我們與神和好的道路，滿足了我們最大的需要。祂應許與我們同在，並賜給我們每天跟隨祂所需的力量（腓 4:13）。記念耶穌的能力和祂對我們的愛，能幫助我們在等待結果時信靠祂。

content.en:
Can you imagine how the Israelites felt as they came up on the body of water? The situation must’ve felt desperate: the Egyptians behind them, the water in front of them, and nowhere to go. Can you picture walking on dry land through the walls of the sea, knowing that just a few minutes earlier, there was no way out? They had been slaves in Egypt for 400 years before God sent Moses to rescue them, so we can understand any confusion they had when God powerfully parted the waters. Not long after this miraculous moment, the people started complaining about hunger, accusing God of leading them into the wilderness to die. As outsiders looking in, we get frustrated with the Israelites and are shocked that they want to go back to Egypt—to slavery. But imagine if they were reading a story about your life and how God has worked to rescue you; would they also get frustrated over how quickly you forget and turn to worldly comforts to satisfy your desires or to fit in?

Why do we so easily forget? Our world, bodies, and minds are broken. Sin easily distracts us with a promise of temporary pleasure, but God is more wonderful than those fleeting moments. By sending Jesus to take the punishment for your sins, He has done more for you than anything the world can offer you. When you call on the Lord for salvation, you become the dwelling place for the Holy Spirit, who works to transform your heart and mind. The next time you find yourself in a desperate situation, remember that the same power that parted the Red Sea is the same power living inside of you.
content.zh-Hant:
你能想像以色列人來到水邊時有甚麼感受嗎？當時的處境一定令人絕望：埃及人在後面，水在前面，無路可走。你能想像自己走在兩邊海水之間的乾地上，知道幾分鐘前還無路可逃嗎？神差遣摩西拯救他們以前，他們在埃及作了四百年的奴隸，因此我們可以理解，當神大能地分開海水時，他們可能感到困惑。這神蹟發生後不久，百姓就開始抱怨飢餓，指責神帶他們到曠野送死。作為旁觀者，我們對以色列人感到沮喪，也驚訝他們想回埃及去作奴隸。但試想，如果他們讀到你生命的故事，以及神如何動工拯救你；他們會不會也因你如此快就忘記，轉向世上的安逸來滿足慾望或融入人群而感到沮喪？

為甚麼我們這麼容易忘記？我們的世界、身體和思想都已破碎。罪以短暫的快樂作為誘惑，很容易使我們分心，但神比那些轉瞬即逝的時刻更美好。祂差遣耶穌承擔你罪的刑罰，為你所做的超過世界能給你的一切。當你呼求主的救恩時，你就成為聖靈的居所；聖靈在你裏面動工，改變你的心思意念。下次陷入絕境時，記得那分開紅海的能力，也住在你裏面。

question.en: When you face a challenging situation, what is the first thing you turn to as a way of escape? Why?
question.zh-Hant: 面對艱難處境時，你首先會轉向甚麼來尋求逃避？為甚麼？

question.en: Recall a Red Sea moment—when you thought that a good outcome was impossible. How did God make a way and work it out?
question.zh-Hant: 回想一個你的紅海時刻——你認為不可能有好結果的時候。神如何開路並使事情得到解決？

prayer.en: God, thank You for all the ways You have rescued me. If all You ever did was save me from my sins, that would be enough. Help me to always remember the signs and wonders You have used to rescue me.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢以各種方式拯救我。即使祢所做的只是把我從罪中拯救出來，也已經足夠。求祢幫助我時常記得祢用來拯救我的神蹟奇事。

content.en:
Most of us don’t immediately trust people we’ve just met. Trusting new people is much easier when another trusted friend has already tested and approved of their character and integrity. In a way, the Bible does this for us. Scripture is full of people who lived lives just like us—who faced moments requiring great faith in God to have their back. Because of these testimonies in Scripture, when you surrender your life to Christ through faith, you aren’t acting in blind faith. God has proven over and over again that He takes care of His people.

Hebrews 11 is known as the “Hall of Faith” because the people listed there faced circumstances beyond their control. Many times, they didn’t know what was going to happen, but they took the next step in faith because they trusted the One guiding their steps. They had unwavering faith in God because they witnessed His unwavering commitment to work all things for their good and His glory (Rom. 8:28).

God is for us; He is committed to us. We can move confidently through the unknown because we know God’s character through the stories in His Word. You can’t see God with your eyes, but your relationship with Him is as real as it gets, as real as your relationship with your closest friend. If you are waiting for a clear sign from God to know if you can trust Him, you can look in His Word. You can confidently move in faith because God has already proven He is faithful to take care of you.
content.zh-Hant:
我們大多不會立刻信任剛認識的人。如果另一位我們信任的朋友已經考驗並肯定了這人的品格和正直，信任新朋友就容易得多。從某個角度來看，聖經為我們做了這件事。聖經中有許多像我們一樣生活的人，他們面對一些時刻，需要對支持他們的神有極大的信心。因著聖經中的這些見證，當你憑信心把生命交給基督時，並不是盲目相信。神一再證明祂會照顧祂的子民。

希伯來書第十一章被稱為「信心名人堂」，因為其中列舉的人面對超出自己掌控的處境。他們多次不知道將會發生甚麼，但因信靠那位引導他們腳步的神，就憑信心踏出下一步。他們對神有堅定不移的信心，因為他們見證了神堅定不移地使萬事為他們的益處和祂的榮耀而效力（羅 8:28）。

神站在我們這邊；祂對我們信實。我們透過神話語中的故事認識祂的品格，因此可以滿有信心地走過未知。你無法用眼睛看見神，但你與祂的關係真實無比，就像你與最親密朋友的關係一樣真實。如果你正等候神給你一個明確的記號，好知道自己能否信靠祂，你可以查考祂的話語。你可以滿有信心地憑信前行，因為神已經證明祂會信實地照顧你。

question.en: Is it easy for you to have faith in God even though you cannot see Him? Why or why not?
question.zh-Hant: 雖然看不見神，你仍容易對祂有信心嗎？為甚麼？

question.en: When have you faced a situation that was beyond your control? In what ways did God take care of you?
question.zh-Hant: 你何時曾面對超出自己掌控的處境？神以甚麼方式照顧你？

prayer.en: Thank You for Your unwavering faithfulness to love and take care of me. I trust that You are working all things for my good, even when I can’t see it. Help me to walk confidently into the unknown because You are there.
prayer.zh-Hant: 感謝祢始終信實地愛我、照顧我。我相信祢使萬事為我的益處效力，即使我看不見。求祢幫助我滿懷信心地走進未知，因為祢在那裏。

content.en:
Have you ever been to a football game in your hometown? An interesting thing happens as the athletes on the field grow up and sit in the stands as adults. People often still see them as who they were when they were students.

Today’s reading is the perfect example of this phenomenon. Jesus met with a Samaritan woman and was flooded with other Samaritans, who were eager to meet Him. The Jews were God’s chosen people from which Jesus descended, and they despised the Samaritans. But Jesus gave them His time and attention anyway. As Jesus left for Galilee, He said that a man does not have honor in his hometown. If Jesus was to sit in the football stands in Galilee, the people would struggle to see Him as anyone other than the boy they watched grow up there. They didn’t give Jesus the honor He deserved. When He arrived in Galilee, some accepted Him only because they had seen His works in Jerusalem. The Samaritans believed without seeing, but the Jews needed to see before they believed.

Jesus’s mission was to save both the Jews and the Gentiles. Anyone lost in sin can call on the name of the Lord and be saved. Though the Jews ultimately rejected Jesus, He became a sacrifice for their sins. His sacrifice was for every person and group, including you.
content.zh-Hant:
你曾在家鄉看過美式足球比賽嗎？當球場上的運動員長大成人，坐在觀眾席上時，會發生一件有趣的事：人們往往仍把他們看成學生時代的模樣。

今天的經文正好說明這種現象。耶穌遇見一位撒馬利亞婦人，隨後許多渴望見祂的撒馬利亞人湧向祂。猶太人是神的選民，耶穌出自他們當中；他們卻鄙視撒馬利亞人。但耶穌仍然花時間關心撒馬利亞人。當耶穌動身前往加利利時，祂說一個人在自己的家鄉不受尊敬。如果耶穌坐在加利利的足球觀眾席上，人們恐怕很難不把祂看成他們看著長大的那個男孩。他們沒有給耶穌應得的尊榮。祂來到加利利時，有些人接待祂，只因看見祂在耶路撒冷所行的事。撒馬利亞人沒有看見就相信了，猶太人卻要先看見才相信。

耶穌的使命是拯救猶太人和外邦人。任何迷失在罪中的人都可以呼求主名而得救。雖然猶太人最終拒絕了耶穌，祂仍為他們的罪成為祭物。祂的犧牲是為了每一個人和每一個群體，包括你。

question.en: Do you only trust God when you have seen Him work? What about when He feels silent?
question.zh-Hant: 你是否只在看見神動工時才信靠祂？當你感覺祂沉默時又如何？

question.en: What sins are you hiding because you fear God can’t or won’t forgive you? Confess them to God today.
question.zh-Hant: 你因害怕神不能或不願赦免而隱藏哪些罪？今天向神承認這些罪。

prayer.en: Thank You, God, for Jesus’s sacrifice for my sins. Thank You for choosing all people to bless with Your mercy and grace. Help me show this love to everyone today.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢，因耶穌為我的罪犧牲。感謝祢揀選以祢的憐憫和恩典祝福萬民。求祢幫助我今天向每個人彰顯這份愛。

content.en:
What is your definition of the word “anything”? As it is used in this Scripture, it encompasses everything; nothing is left out. Think back to this week’s lesson. The father was desperate for his son’s healing. When Jesus told him that his son was healed, the man believed, even though he hadn’t seen his son yet.

When you read, “Do not be anxious about anything,” your mind may go to a situation that is the exception. You may feel like your situation is beyond help, even from God. You may believe that God can work things out for other people, but your case is different, too difficult.

What Scripture says is true: No situation in your life is too far out of God’s reach for Him to take care of. Everything means everything. The Scripture goes on to say that you only need to turn over everything to God through prayer. He cares. He wants to meet you where you are. He wants to take the burden you are carrying and replace your anxiety with peace. When you let go of control and give it over to God, the peace that surpasses all understanding will cover your mind and dissolve the worry. Because of Jesus and with the help of the Holy Spirit, we have access to peace. You can’t do anything to earn it; instead, the God of all creation sees you, cares about you, and takes care of you. He sent Jesus to create a way for you to experience His peace. You must simply believe.
content.zh-Hant:
你如何理解這段經文中「一無掛慮」的「一無」？它涵蓋一切，沒有任何遺漏。回想本週的課程。那位父親迫切盼望兒子得醫治。當耶穌告訴他兒子得醫治時，他雖然還沒有看見兒子，卻相信了。

當你讀到「應當一無掛慮」時，你可能會想到一個例外的處境。你可能覺得自己的處境無人能幫，連神也不能。你可能相信神能為別人解決問題，但你的情況不同，太困難了。

聖經所說的是真實的：你生命中沒有任何處境超出神照顧的範圍。凡事就是一切。經文接著說，你只需要藉著禱告把一切交給神。祂關心你，願意在你的處境中與你相遇。祂願意擔負你的重擔，以平安取代你的憂慮。當你放下控制權，把一切交給神，那超越人所能理解的平安就會遮蓋你的心思，消除憂慮。因著耶穌，也藉著聖靈的幫助，我們可以得到平安。你無法靠任何行為賺取平安；創造萬有的神看見你、關心你，也照顧你。祂差遣耶穌，為你開了一條經歷祂平安的道路。你只需要相信。

question.en: Recall a time when you felt desperate for God’s peace in a situation. Did you give it over to Him through prayer? How did He provide peace?
question.zh-Hant: 回想一次你在某個處境中迫切需要神的平安。你是否藉禱告把它交給祂？祂如何賜下平安？

question.en: Do you believe that God cares for you and wants to take care of you in every situation? Why or why not?
question.zh-Hant: 你相信神關心你，並願意在每個處境中照顧你嗎？為甚麼？

prayer.en: God, You see me, You know me, and You care about me. And I’m grateful. Thank You for Your peace in all situations—even the ones that cause anxiety to rise in my mind. I give it all to You. Thank You for taking it from me.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，祢看見我、認識我，也關心我，我十分感恩。感謝祢在一切處境中賜下平安，包括那些使我心生憂慮的處境。我把一切交給祢。感謝祢為我擔負。

content.en:
What is the most painful situation or season you have ever been in? Was finding meaning in it easy or difficult? Your hardest, most desperate situations can be used for good and for God’s glory. Saying we believe this is easy, but actually believing it is more difficult when you’re in the middle of desperate times. Those times test whether or not we believe what we claim. In today’s passage, the father learns that his son was healed in the same moment Jesus said he was healed. This moment could have easily been overlooked or missed. In today’s culture, we tend to believe that miracles like this don’t happen. How often do we miss the opportunity to point others to Jesus because we do not see Jesus’s work happening right in front of us?

This father didn’t miss it; he knew Jesus had healed his son. The most painful moment of his life was redeemed by Jesus, and he told everyone about it. We can use this story as a model for us to imitate: The father invited Jesus into a very desperate situation because he knew Jesus was the only One who could fix it. Then, he invited everyone else into the story so that they could see that Jesus could help them too.

What about you? What painful situation are you in right now, and how have you looked to Jesus to redeem it? Friend, Jesus redeeming the hardest seasons of your life is just as possible for you as it was for this young boy and his father. The next step for you is simple: Invite Jesus to fix it, and then tell anyone who will listen about His goodness.
content.zh-Hant:
你曾經歷最痛苦的處境或時期是甚麼？要在其中找到意義是容易還是困難？你最艱難、最絕望的處境可以被用來帶來益處和神的榮耀。說我們相信這一點很容易，但真正身處絕境時，要相信就困難多了。那些時刻考驗我們是否相信自己所宣稱的。今天的經文中，父親得知兒子正是在耶穌說他會活的那一刻得醫治。這一刻很容易被忽略或錯過。在今天的文化中，我們傾向認為這樣的神蹟不會發生。我們有多少次因為看不見耶穌正在眼前動工，而錯過了引領別人認識祂的機會？

這位父親沒有錯過；他知道耶穌醫治了他的兒子。他生命中最痛苦的時刻被耶穌救贖，他就把這事告訴眾人。我們可以把這故事作為效法的榜樣：這位父親邀請耶穌進入極其絕望的處境，因為他知道只有耶穌能解決。然後，他邀請其他人進入這故事，讓他們看見耶穌也能幫助他們。

你呢？你現在正身處甚麼痛苦的處境？你如何仰望耶穌來救贖這處境？朋友，耶穌救贖你生命中最艱難的時期，對你而言也同樣可能，正如對這男孩和他的父親一樣。你的下一步很簡單：邀請耶穌解決問題，然後向願意聆聽的人述說祂的良善。

question.en: Do you struggle to allow God to use your difficult seasons for your good and His glory? Explain.
question.zh-Hant: 你是否難以讓神使用你艱難的時期，帶來你的益處和祂的榮耀？請解釋。

question.en: Recall a time when you or someone you know went through a painful time but were able to use it to spread the gospel. What does this show you about our pain?
question.zh-Hant: 回想一次你或你認識的人經歷痛苦時期，卻能藉此傳揚福音。這讓你對我們的痛苦有甚麼認識？

prayer.en: Thank You, God, for working all things for my good and Your glory. You are the only One who can redeem my pain. Please give me the courage to use difficult situations in my life to spread the message of Your goodness and grace.
prayer.zh-Hant: 神啊，感謝祢使萬事為我的益處和祢的榮耀效力。唯有祢能救贖我的痛苦。求祢賜給我勇氣，使用生命中的艱難處境，傳揚祢良善和恩典的信息。
